 Caterpillar’s 34% Slump Over 6 Months: Wall Street Desk Says It Sets Up 90% Gains Within a Year
 By Alex Sirois 
 Published November 16, 2026, 10:45am ET · 3 min read 
 𝕏 
 f 
 ⧉ 
 Quick Read
 Caterpillar's record $78 billion backlog, fueled by data center power demand, hasn't stopped a 32% six-month slide, leaving analysts' average target implying 36% upside.
 Deere gained 5% over the past month while PACCAR slipped 4%, so Caterpillar's discount looks tied to AI spending fears, not machinery weakness.
 CEO Joe Creed is taking "turbine orders into 2030," and the next earnings call's 2027 plans are the clearest near-term catalyst.

 Caterpillar ( NYSE:CAT | CAT Price Prediction ) currently trades at $600.18. The average analyst price target is $815.26, which means 35.8% upside.
 Caterpillar builds construction and mining equipment, but Wall Street now pays most attention to its turbines and large engines that power data centers. Its backlog hit a record $78 billion [ 1 ] , up 96% from a year earlier. Even so, shares have fallen 32.15% over six months. The highest target on the Street, $1,150.00, means roughly 91.6% upside.

 AI Jitters and a Soft Outlook Sent Caterpillar Down 32%
 The selling started when investors turned on AI stocks, and Caterpillar had become one of the industrial names tied to that trade. Shares were on track to fall. Bloomberg reported a decline of more than 30% from their record high as oil prices, bond yields and doubts about AI spending weighed on industrials.
 The third-quarter report made things worse. Revenue of $20.68 billion [ 2 ] came in line with the $20.69 billion estimate, and management forecast to “moderate sales growth” [ 1 ] in the fourth quarter. Over the past 30 days, analysts cut their fourth-quarter EPS estimates 10 times and raised them only 2 times. Management also said adjusted operating margins, excluding tariff recoveries, will land near the bottom of its target range.
 Most of the damage was specific to Caterpillar. The stock dropped 19.68% in a month, while the S&P 500 slipped 1.16%.
 Analysts Are Holding Firm on Orders Booked Into 2030
 Analysts see demand running ahead of what Caterpillar can build. Power generation sales to users grew 75% [ 1 ] . CEO Joe Creed said the company is “taking some large reciprocating orders as far out as 2029 and turbine orders into 2030.” [ 1 ] Adjusted EPS of $7.20 [ 2 ] beat the $7.04 consensus. Analysts expect EPS to rise from $27.1117 this year to $32.247 next year. Creed expects to “claw our way off the bottom of that margin target range” [ 1 ] and will lay out 2027 plans on the next earnings call. That call is the clearest near-term catalyst.
 Of 29 analysts, 2 give the stock a Strong Buy rating, 15 a Buy, 11 a Hold, and 1 a Sell. Recent target changes have been cuts: Citigroup ( NYSE:C ) lowered its target to $1,000 and Freedom Broker lowered its target to $800, both to account for dealers reducing their inventories. Price targets are 12-month opinions, and the distance between the average target and the Street high shows how far apart those opinions are.
 Deere and PACCAR Sidestepped Caterpillar’s Slide
 Caterpillar’s closest machinery peers held up much better, so this selloff stands mostly alone.
 Deere ( NYSE:DE ) rose 4.94% over the past month and is up 44.67% year to date. With shares at $673.54 and a $694.01 average target, analysts see just 3.0% upside. Its ratings consist of 5 Strong Buy, 11 Buy, and 9 Hold, with no Sells.
 PACCAR ( NASDAQ:PCAR ) slipped 3.75% over the month. With the stock at $106.66 versus a $125.10 target, implied upside is 17.3%. Analysts are more conservative here: 9 of its 19 analysts rate it Hold.
 Caterpillar has the largest analyst-implied upside of the three, which suggests its discount comes from fears about AI spending, while the broader machinery business is holding up.
 Caterpillar Trails the S&P 500 Despite a Positive Year
 Caterpillar currently trades at $600.18 against an average target of $815.26 from 29 analysts, means 35.8% upside. Shares are down 32.15% over six months, although they rebounded 7.44% in the latest week.
 Year to date, the stock is up 5.67%, while the S&P 500 is up 10.62%. Caterpillar trades at about 19 times forward earnings and sits well below its 52-week high of $1,068.93.
 Caterpillar Looks Like an Opportunity if 2027 Margins Deliver
 Caterpillar looks like an opportunity here. Data center power orders need to keep turning into shipments, and the 2027 outlook should show margins moving up from the bottom of the target range. A record backlog and a forward multiple near 19 give the stock a credible path back toward $815.26.
 The bull case weakens if AI spending actually slows. Customers can push back long-dated turbine orders, tariff costs will run about $2.2 billion [ 1 ] this year, and analysts are already cutting fourth-quarter estimates. If that happens, the $1,150.00 high target will look like a leftover from peak enthusiasm.
 I lean toward opportunity. The selloff assumes an AI slowdown that has not yet shown up in Caterpillar’s orders, and the 2027 plans on the next earnings call will show whether that view holds up.
